basics.name: Martha Fey
basics.label: Environmental Health | Statistical Analysis | Research
basics.summary: University of Iowa graduate with interests in environmental health, statistical analysis, drinking water quality, and the relationship between environmental conditions and human health. Experienced in environmental monitoring, research instrumentation, data collection, and quantitative analysis.

work.name: Benton County Environmental Health
work.summary: Conduct environmental health work focused on private drinking water wells and communicating water quality results to property owners.
highlights: Collect and test private well water samples.
Explain water quality results and provide recommendations to property owners.
Developed a study concept using R to examine whether well characteristics, including age, depth, and condition, are associated with water sample results.

work.name: Harsco Environmental
work.summary: Supported safety training and documentation at an industrial materials recovery operation.
highlights: Converted written operating procedures into interactive training materials.
Organized safety training materials and tracked participation.
Worked with standard operating procedures, job safety analyses, risk assessments, and training resources.

work.name: University of Iowa
work.summary: Contributed to prairie restoration and climate research examining environmental processes related to carbon cycling.
highlights: Constructed an eddy covariance flux tower with faculty guidance for environmental monitoring and prairie restoration research.
Integrated instrument wiring, solar power, battery backup, and wireless data transmission.
Supported environmental data collection and processing for research on land management and climate strategies.
Contributed to a collaborative research manuscript examining the biogeophysical cooling potential of constructed prairie.
Graduated in the top 5% of the class.

volunteer.organization: International Student Support / OASIS, University of Iowa
highlights: Helped coordinate multicultural events attended by more than 400 people.
Supported programming and community engagement for international students.

publications.name: Assessing the Biogeophysical Cooling Potential of Constructed Prairie with Eddy Covariance and Thermal UAS Remote Sensing
publications.summary: Collaborative research examining the cooling potential of constructed prairie using eddy covariance and thermal remote sensing.
